text: Lemma 9 [on paper]. Let $G$ be metabelian of class $c$, $k=c-1$, $x_i^{E_i}=P_i\in\gamma_k$, and $E_iE_j\mid A_{ij}$. Then $u_{ij}=1$. Hence $w\ne1$ forces $E_iE_j\nmid A_{ij}$ for some $i<j$ (for powers of two: $A_{ij}<E_iE_j$). Proof. $u_{ij}=[x_i,P_j^{q}]=[x_i,P_j]^q$, $q=A_{ij}/E_j$, since $[x_i,P_j]\in\gamma_c$ is central; and $[x_i,P_j]^{E_i}=[x_i^{E_i},P_j]=[P_i,P_j]=1$ ($\gamma_k\subseteq G'$ is abelian). $\square$

text: So in (3.12) the pairing does not see $x_5$ at all (the same multipliers, the same exactness, in $M$ and in $G$), and $S\in\Delta^6$ with or without it. What $x_5$ does [computer]: it puts $128X_2^2X_1=2E_2\,X_2^2X_1$ into $\Delta^6$ (the pairing lemma alone gives $\Delta^5$), hence $B_{12}\in\Delta^6$, and it makes $B_{13}+B_{23}\in\Delta^6$ although neither term is. Dropping only its power relator $x_5^{1024}d_2^{16}$ undoes the first effect. The lift is exactly one level: at $n=7$, $128X_2^2X_1\notin\Delta^7$ in c4a (CPU, 3.8 h on a shared machine, certificate holds; c4a_lin2_n7.log). (Which identity in $\mathbb Z[G]$ does it, was not found on paper.) L2g fails at $n=7$ in $S$ (multiplier 1 where 4 is needed) and in every $B_{ij}$.

It is a lower bound for the true level; relators can do better.

text: Lemma 10 [on paper]. Let $E_i\le E_j$, $A=A_{ij}=2^\alpha<E_iE_j$ (the pair of Lemma 9). The certified level of $\binom A2X_j^2X_i$ is at most $k+2=c+1$. Proof. $v_2\binom A2=\alpha-1\le a_i+a_j-2$. Raising $X_j$ to level $\ge2$ costs $\ge a_j$, and then $\le a_i-2<a_i$ is left: the other two factors stay at level 1, total $\le k+2$. Otherwise only $X_i$ is raised, to $\le k$: total $\le k+2$. $\square$
